title: Climate and disaster information integrity work remains concentrated on detection and response while prevention, recovery, and community approaches lag
source_unit: UNDP, Frontiers of Information Integrity in Climate Change and Climate-Related Disasters: Information Integrity Interventions Landscape Report, 11 September 2026
geography: Global climate-change and climate-related-disaster information ecosystems and intervention landscape

denominator.unit: UNDP landscape mapping of several hundred information-integrity interventions, including almost fifty climate/disaster-focused interventions

intervention_scope.value: the report maps several hundred information-integrity interventions across thematic areas, including almost fifty focused on climate change and climate-related disasters

challenge_scope.value: the landscape examines misinformation, disinformation, and other information pollution affecting climate action and disaster response

actor_scope.value: the mapping identifies patterns in challenges, strategies, approaches, and actors involved

information_route.value: climate resilience increasingly depends on the integrity of the information environment through which risk, action, and recovery are interpreted

observations.method: UNDP landscape report mapping several hundred information-integrity interventions and comparing climate-specific practice with other policy areas.
observations.uncertainty: The report examines intervention design and positioning; it does not assess the effectiveness of individual interventions or explain why some intervention types are more prevalent.
observations.subgroup: Climate communicators, disaster responders, governments, platforms, media, civil society, communities, funders, and people exposed to climate hazards.
observations.counterinterpretation: A concentration on detection and response may reflect the maturity of available tools rather than an intentional neglect of prevention or recovery.

observations.period: 2026; intervention imbalance across the disaster cycle

detection_response.value: climate-related information-integrity efforts are concentrated largely on detection and response

prevention_gap.value: prevention, recovery, and community-based approaches are less prominent

cycle_route.value: information integrity is being handled more as an incident-response function than as a continuous preparedness, adaptation, and recovery capability

open_test.value: track whether prevention, recovery, and community-led information practices improve warning, preparedness, action, and post-disaster learning

observations.method: UNDP comparative analysis of climate-specific intervention types and approaches.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not estimate the effectiveness, funding, reach, or causal contribution of detection, response, prevention, recovery, or community approaches.
observations.subgroup: Hazard-exposed communities, emergency managers, local governments, journalists, platforms, fact-checkers, and climate organizations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Detection and response may be prerequisites for later prevention and recovery systems, especially where climate misinformation is fast-moving or crisis-driven.

observations.period: 2026; structural gaps in climate information ecosystems

platform_gap.value: the report identifies gaps related to platform participation

regional_gap.value: regional coordination remains a structural gap

funding_gap.value: sustainable funding is insufficiently connected to climate and disaster information-integrity work

digital_community_gap.value: digital approaches are not consistently connected to community-based approaches

governance_route.value: climate information integrity depends on coordination across platforms, regions, funders, digital systems, and communities

observations.method: UNDP intervention-landscape synthesis of actors, strategies, thematic approaches, and ecosystem gaps.
observations.uncertainty: The identified gaps are landscape findings, not quantified measures of funding deficits, platform behavior, regional capacity, or community outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Local and national governments, platforms, funders, community groups, regional bodies, responders, and vulnerable populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some coordination and funding may occur outside the mapped interventions or through informal networks not visible in the landscape.

observations.period: 2026; implications for climate action and disaster response

denominator.unit: key conclusions reported by the landscape study

policy_translation.value: the report ends with nine conclusions intended to inform future policy, programming, partnerships, and research

public_action.value: information pollution can affect how people understand climate risk, respond to disaster warnings, and support or resist climate action

trust_route.value: information integrity is part of the social infrastructure required for collective agreement and coordinated climate response

boundary.value: the publication offers a landscape and research agenda rather than evidence that any intervention changed behavior or reduced disaster harm

observations.method: UNDP landscape report conclusions based on intervention mapping and comparative analysis.
observations.uncertainty: The conclusions are directional and programmatic; effectiveness and causal pathways remain open research questions.
observations.subgroup: Climate-policy publics, disaster-affected communities, information intermediaries, emergency services, researchers, and policymakers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Material preparedness, trusted local institutions, and direct experience may sometimes outweigh information pollution in shaping response.

related_sources.claim: UNDP's information-integrity portfolio provides broader open-public-sphere and institutional-trust context.
UNFCCC culture-and-climate strategy provides complementary public-engagement and climate-storytelling context.

boundary: This record adds an information-integrity route from climate and disaster misinformation, disinformation, and information pollution through preparedness, public action, response, recovery, trust, and coordination. It is a mapped intervention landscape, not an effectiveness evaluation, event dataset, behavioral study, or proof of causality between information pollution and climate outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNDP publication page and indexed report summary were reviewed for intervention-map scope, detection/response concentration, prevention/recovery/community gaps, structural ecosystem gaps, nine conclusions, and effectiveness limitations.
